short: Closed-loop word synthesis (M06) from a chronic ECoG implant in ALS (M13) holds on six keywords at 80% listener accuracy; standard designs, one participant, stability untested.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06: closed loop, each word decoded with look-ahead and played after it ends) and the setting (M13: chronic ECoG in a speaker with ALS, 5.5 months after training). Both are standard by the rules: closed-loop neural synthesis existed in 3 of 50 prior studies [@guenther2009; @brumberg2018; @angrick2021], and one participant with pooled sessions gives no repetition. The main claim holds narrowly: six keywords were identified at 80% against 16.7% chance, the earliest intelligible closed-loop neural synthesis in the prior set, obtained by dropping the real-time constraint and closing the vocabulary. The stability claim has no pre-gap comparison, and synthesized words remain far less intelligible than the participant's own speech (99.8%).
